questions.question: Define direct distance and explain why the road distance between two towns in a mountainous area is usually much longer than the direct distance.
questions.expected_answer: Direct distance is the straight-line distance between two points on a map, as the crow flies. In mountainous areas roads must wind around and over mountains, follow valleys and use passes, so the road is much longer than the straight line.

questions.question: On a map with the scale 1 cm represents 25 km, two towns are 8.4 cm apart. Estimate the distance, calculate it accurately, and show the full-marks layout.
questions.expected_answer: Estimate: about 8 x 25 = about 200 km. Map distance 8.4 cm; scale 1 cm represents 25 km; 8.4 x 25 = 210; direct distance = 210 km.

questions.question: Give three checks you should carry out after calculating a distance and two common errors.
questions.expected_answer: Checks: compare with the estimate; check the units are sensible; measure again; compare with another source such as an atlas or map app. Errors: measuring from the end of the ruler instead of zero; measuring to the edge of labels; dividing instead of multiplying; not converting mm to cm; no units.
